newsitem.title: USA: AMP cautious on 1997, sees Q1 sales pick-up.
newsitem.headline: AMP cautious on 1997, sees Q1 sales pick-up.

text.p: AMP Inc said it remains cautious on economic and market conditions for 1997, but expects an improvement in local currency sales growth during the year.

In a statement accompanying its fourth quarter earnings release, the company said it expected the first quarter of 1997 to set a new high in sales and some improvement in operating earnings compared to the fourth quarter.
AMP reported operating earnings of $0.40 per share in the fourth quarter versus $0.52 per share in the year-ago quarter. The $0.40 figure was $0.03 shy of the First Call consensus.

AMP said it would segment its engineering costs and include a portion of these expenses in its standard costs, leading to a revaluation of inventory resulting in a one-time gain of about $0.10 to $0.15 a share in the first quarter.
However, it warned that if foreign currency levels remain at current levels, they will have a negative effect on first quarter and year results.
In addition, AMP said capital expenditures for 1996 dropped to $592 million from $713 million in 1995 and such spending was likely to stay at levels similar to 1996 during the current year.
AMP also said 1996 bookings of $1.37 billion were up from $1.33 billion in the third quarter of 1996 but order backlog fell $30 million during the fourth quarter to $970 million.

The company had announced in late December that it expected earnings "similar" to the $0.43 per share reported in the fourth quarter of 1996 and planned to take restructuring charges of $195 million during the fourth quarter.
On January 8, it detailed a series of restructuring actions that it said would result in 1,000 net job losses worldwide and annual cost savings of about $50 million a year.

The company, the world's leading maker of electronic connectors, said it took a $195 million pre-tax charge in the fourth quarter of 1996 to cover the restructuring and other special items, $125 million of which was non-cash in nature.
It said the actions should not be considered a general downsizing, but simply a response to declining earnings in the second half of 1996 and a bid to cut losses in certain units.
AMP stated that, "We believe the basic strategy we are following -- maintain connector leadership, diversify into related product/market sectors, and expand globally -- is sound."
"The corrective actions we are taking are specific adjustments and not a change in direction," the statement added.
It said that fourth quarter sales of $1.4 billion rose from the $1.3 billion reported in the third quarter, while margins decreased slightly.

AMP said earnings were hurt by a number of factors including underutilization of capacity in some facilities, price erosion, rising depreciation charges, inventory adjustments, and adverse currency effects.
It labelled 1996 a "disappointing" year. Sales of $5.47 billion were up only 7 percent in local currencies and 5 percent in U.S. dollars, much less than it had expected at the outset of 1996.
AMP said U.S. dollar strength cut sales by $145 million.
It said U.S. sales, 44 percent of AMP's total, were up 8 percent, with strongest growth in the automotive and power/utilities markets.
